title: Radians, arcs and segments
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point also covers radian measure and segment areas, which neither bank point teaches fully: mat-arcs-sectors lacks segments and mat-radians lacks arc length and sector area, so no single bank point matches it.

draft.title: Radians, arcs and segments
card: One radian is the angle at the centre of a circle when the arc is as long as the radius. A half turn is π radians, so π radians = 180°.
To change degrees to radians, multiply by π/180. To change radians to degrees, multiply by 180/π.
With θ in radians, arc length = rθ and sector area = ½r²θ. These formulas only work when θ is in radians.
A segment is a sector with its triangle removed. The triangle has area ½r² sin θ, so segment area = ½r²(θ − sin θ). Example: r = 6 and θ = π/3 give arc length 2π and sector area 6π.
draft.remember: Use radians in the formulas: arc = rθ, sector = ½r²θ, segment = sector − triangle.

a.q: A sector of a circle has radius 5 cm and centre angle 2 radians. What is its arc length?
a.why: Arc length = rθ = 5 × 2 = 10 cm. The value 25 comes from the sector area formula ½r²θ, which gives an area in cm², not a length.
a.clue: Multiply the radius by the angle in radians.

b.q: A circle has radius 4 cm. A chord cuts off a segment with centre angle π/2. What is the area of the segment?
b.why: Sector = ½ × 16 × π/2 = 4π. Triangle = ½ × 16 × sin(π/2) = 8. Segment = 4π − 8 cm². Choosing 4π gives the whole sector, which still includes the triangle.
b.clue: Take the triangle's area away from the sector's area.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's worked example, both questions and both explanations are correct.
